races.name: C.J. Sheeran Ltd 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown from John Joseph Hanlon's yard with no hurdles form to dissect; running style unclassified, which leaves this a pure speculative entry — could land anywhere in the field, and its chance hinges entirely on raw ability translating first time over hurdles at this trip.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: Last seen finishing ninth of seventeen at Ballinrobe over this course and distance on Good ground, which is a poor reference; a natural hold-up operator whose style is compressed into midfield by the sheer volume of similar types, diluting its chance in a shape where ground is not easily recovered.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Six runs over obstacles without a win and never better than sixth in hurdles company; natural rear-end racing style sits awkwardly in a field already saturated with hold-up horses, and William Durkan's yard has been cold (0 wins from 11 in the past 14 days), adding a second layer of concern.

runners_data.name: Minella Buoy
runners_data.note: Ran second over this exact course and distance on Good ground last time, which is the most directly relevant piece of form in the race; a genuine hold-up type but squeezed into midfield by field composition — if it can find daylight in the closing stages its sim-going record (2nd of 5 on similar ground) makes it interesting.

runners_data.name: Motherland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's entry is completely unknown over hurdles and the running style is unclassified, but the trainer's 2 wins from 46 in the past 14 days keeps expectations measured; with no form ceiling to speak of, this has to be respected as a dark horse on maiden hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Mount Eden
runners_data.note: Showed a placing at Ballinrobe over 2m on Good ground but has faded at the finish in subsequent starts; a natural hold-up runner operating out of role in a field loaded with similar types, and the fades-in-finish flag is a specific worry at this stamina-testing trip.

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent racer in the field aside from Words Unspoken, giving Sean Flanagan the ability to sit just off the leader's shoulder and control his own race; ran third at Ballinrobe over 2m on Good last time and has placed three times in six starts, making this the most tactically well-placed rival to the leader.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's charge has run seven times without winning and showed an eleven-length eleventh at Ballinrobe over this trip last time, the most recent form reading poorly; hold-up profile is natural but the track form here is discouraging.

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race, able to bowl along uncontested under Phillip Enright from flag to finish; both hurdles runs have come at Ballinrobe on Good ground, providing course-and-distance familiarity, and the absence of any pace rival makes its controlling role essentially uncontested.

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner has never threatened in six runs, with form figures of 7-8-7-7-12 including two outings on Good ground; naturally a rear-track racer working out of its preferred position given field composition, and zero wins or places in sim-going runs makes this difficult to support.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Ran fourth of seventeen at Ballinrobe on Good ground on debut over hurdles which is the key piece of form, wearing a tongue-tie throughout; a hold-up type whose natural position is compressed by field dynamics, though the tongue-tie and Gavin Cromwell's patient placing keeps it relevant.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Has a placing on Good ground (2nd of ten over 2m) buried among otherwise poor efforts; a hold-up type who has faded in finishes previously, and Conor Lamon's 7lb claim offers minor weight relief but doesn't address the core structural issue of too many hold-up rivals chasing the same ground.

runners_data.name: Sofi's Gift
runners_data.note: Ran second at Ballinrobe on Good ground over 2m last time, giving it a direct course and distance placing of note; a natural hold-up type crammed into midfield by field composition, but the recent good form gives Ciaran Murphy's charge an each-way profile if traffic clears in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Words Unspoken is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 3-Y-O maiden hurdle at Ballinrobe, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Phillip Enright can dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop over 2m½f on Good ground. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Mount Eden, Minella Buoy, Divine Believer, Connor Of Mali, Divelment, Sofi's Gift, No Bother Aoife, Sands Castle and Nod Of Approval all carry natural rear or hold-up profiles, creating a race shape where the vast majority of the field will be chasing from off the pace. Nicky Larson is the only genuine prominent racer to provide any company to Words Unspoken, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured or artificially inflated. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or make their own running, as the solo leader controls tempo and the bunched hold-up brigade face a difficult task picking through traffic on a turning track; the field holds far more genuine hold-up types than can all settle at the rear, with Mount Eden, Minella Buoy and Divine Believer among those most likely unable to secure their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Words Unspoken is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop and is not reeled in by the prominent horses before the final flight.
scenarios.body: Words Unspoken controls every fraction from the front, setting a rhythm that suits its own stamina and leaves the hold-up brigade with ground to make up on a track that doesn't reward wide runs; Nicky Larson, tracking closely, is best placed to challenge if the leader weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Words Unspoken's lead is eroded approaching the last and a prominent-tracking rival delivers a decisive challenge on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Nicky Larson or an unknown unknown like Camp Verde or Motherland — both lightly raced and unencumbered by a defined hold-up tag — can slot just behind the leader and produce a fresh turn of foot; Good ground and a straightforward pace suit horses who travel with the race rather than against it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected early and creates genuine gaps in the final stages, allowing a hold-up runner to thread through.
scenarios.body: Minella Buoy showed a placing last time out and has the highest sim-going form strike rate among the redistrubted types, making it the most likely beneficiary if traffic clears; however, the out-of-role mapping of most hold-up horses here means this scenario is structurally disadvantaged, and the Ballinrobe track's tight turns limit late swoops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Chaos Breaks
scenarios.trigger: If the large field of 13 runners causes significant interference at hurdles, disrupting the rhythm of the leader and creating an unsettled contest.
scenarios.body: A chaotic race with fallers or checked horses could compress the field and produce a surprising result from a lightly-raced unknown such as Motherland (Gordon Elliott) or Camp Verde (John Joseph Hanlon), both of whom carry no obvious form ceiling; this scenario is low probability but non-zero given maiden hurdle inexperience across the board.

watchPoints.text: Words Unspoken sets every fraction unchallenged — if Phillip Enright controls the tempo, the entire field faces a chase from off the pace and Words Unspoken becomes the key race-shaping horse to monitor throughout.

Nicky Larson is the only prominent-style rival who can legitimately track Words Unspoken — watch whether Sean Flanagan elects to sit on the leader's back or allows a gap, as that decision dictates whether the lead is ever threatened before the last.

Minella Buoy's second at this course and distance last time is the standout piece of form among the hold-up horses — watch whether Daniel King can find a route through from midfield given Ballinrobe's tight, turning track, which severely limits late runs.

With nine of thirteen runners carrying natural hold-up profiles compressed into midfield, the race is at serious risk of traffic congestion approaching the final hurdle — watch for interference and checked horses in the straight affecting multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

Both Camp Verde and Motherland are complete unknowns on hurdles debut — watch market moves close to the off for either, as stable confidence in lightly-raced types from Hanlon and Elliott respectively can be a reliable early indicator.

races.name: Bank Of Ireland Brendan Maloney Memorial Maiden Hurdle
Cummins Homevalue Hardware Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Long Gone
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist on a 57-day break wearing a visor, with solid Good-ground form and three wins at the trip — needs things to go wrong up front to get competitive from his rear position; trainer T14 strike rate of 1/9 is modest.|

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who won over 16f on Good going 25 days ago — recent sharp form is the key angle but dropping back from a flat win to hurdling and a wide runner count may see him swamped; jockey Eoin Walsh takes the ride for a small yard.|

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old hold-up type for Thomas Mullins, clocking a win over this exact 16f trip on Good 21 days ago — only six runs under similar conditions but showed ability when fresh; amateur jockey (5lb claimer) is a mild negative.|

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent-racing type who has placed twice over this trip on Good ground and is only 4 days off his last run, suggesting he is cherry-ripe fitness-wise; Ross O'Sullivan yard is 0/27 in T14 but the horse's style means he should at least get his natural position here.|

runners_data.name: Ripsnorter
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the field; won over 16f on Good going and Danny Mullins gives him the top riding connection — uncontested lead is near-certain and at this trip on this surface he has the profile to exploit it; a six-length or more win at this track over the same conditions last year underpins the case.|

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: A hold-up type wearing a tongue-tie who won over 16f on Good; Alan King takes a 7lb claim and the young age (4) is a slight query over hurdles in a competitive handicap — likely to be caught in the midfield scrum alongside several redistributed rivals.|

runners_data.name: Fremantle Doctor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced on Good ground with two places from 12 runs at similar conditions — returning from 161 days off for John McConnell, whose T14 figures (2/29) suggest horses arrive fit but the layoff is a concern; a genuine back-of-the-field horse who will find himself squeezed into midfield in this shape, limiting his chance.|

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: Won on Good going and placed twice at this trip for John Patrick Ryan, and ran just 7 days ago so fitness is not in question — by nature a confirmed hold-up horse, he will be forced closer to the pace than ideal given the crowded rear, and his STYLE_FIT flag suggests discounting him if the race is run to suit a more forward type.|

runners_data.name: Atlantic Gamble
runners_data.note: Five runs, zero wins or places on Good ground according to his sim-going record — a true hold-up type who has never threatened on this surface, and his natural position at the rear will be further compromised by the congested field map; the 76-day gap compounds the worry.|

runners_data.name: Final Decision
runners_data.note: A prominent-profile horse with three places and a win in similar conditions for PJ Rothwell, and the trainer's T14 figures (2/23) show runners arrive in reasonable fettle — 86 days off is the main concern but if forward enough from the start he can sit just off Ripsnorter and deliver a late challenge.|

runners_data.name: Koeur A Prendre
runners_data.note: Back-to-back seconds over 20f on Good going are striking — Daniel King takes the ride for a small yard and the horse is a natural hold-up type who will need the pace to truly collapse to get competitive; his recent form at the distance is the best angle here even if the race shape is against him.|

runners_data.name: Brave Crogha
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with a visor, returning from 76 days off, who has finished no better than 9th in 13 runs on Good ground — the sim-going record is damning and even getting his ideal position at the rear of the field would not resolve the form concern.|

runners_data.name: Theanniversary Man
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good going in his form string but placed only 7th in his last run at this trip, and his natural hold-up style will be displaced into midfield — 31 days since last run is fine but the yard is 0/4 in T14 and the redistribution cost is real given his STYLE_FIT flag.|

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Oliver McKiernan's hold-up specialist is wearing blinkers and a tongue-tie with a second on Good ground 52 days ago — his sim-going record (6/15 runners ahead) is workable, and he carries the highest STYLE_FIT score among the redistributed horses (0.93), meaning his chances of overcoming positional compromise are marginally better than most of his similarly-displaced rivals.|

races.paceDynamic: Ripsnorter is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the outside, Danny Mullins should be able to dictate a controlled, even tempo on Good ground over 2m½f at Ballinrobe. Go To Town and Final Decision are the only horses with prominent profiles to provide any company in the early stages, but neither is a natural front-runner and neither looks likely to force a truly searching gallop. The result is a race that shapes as a modestly-run lead scenario where the pace is honest but not punishing, giving the field a chance to travel through and making the home turn the critical moment — a profile that suits horses who can travel prominently or make a mid-race move rather than those who need a genuine end-to-end test. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically be accommodated at the rear: Fremantle Doctor, Le Diablo, Atlantic Gamble, Koeur A Prendre, Brave Crogha, Theanniversary Man and Chemdawg are all true hold-up operators redistributed to midfield on the map, but in a race run at this tempo the horses most likely to secure their natural position and benefit are those already mapped at or near the front — Ripsnorter, Go To Town and Final Decision — with the closer brigade squeezed into a congested midfield chase.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ripsnorter Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Ripsnorter dictates an uncontested lead at a controlled pace and kicks early on the home turn.
scenarios.body: Danny Mullins nurses Ripsnorter through a steady first half before quickening the tempo approaching the final hurdles, and with no rival ever having the pace to pressure him, the 5-year-old's front-running form at this trip on Good ground proves decisive. Horses who can travel close to the pace and pick him up late, rather than those making up significant ground, are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just honest enough that Ripsnorter ties up late and one of the prominent-to-midfield types swamps him after the last.
scenarios.body: Go To Town or Final Decision, tracking the early leader with cover, finds the gap on the home turn and outstays a mildly-flattening Ripsnorter over the final two hurdles. This shape suits a horse with a prominent racing style who conserves energy in transit then delivers a clean finishing effort — not the true hold-up brigade who are too far back to reach.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Makes Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses dramatically and the field concertinas, allowing a well-positioned midfield horse to sweep through.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected early gallop or jumping errors at the front cause the pace to fall apart in the straight, giving a horse in the upper midfield — Long Gone, Koeur A Prendre or Le Diablo — a clear run to pick up the pieces. Note that most true hold-up horses in this field are redistributed from their natural rear position, limiting the pool of genuine beneficiaries to the more forward-placed midfielders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments due to fallers, unseats or significant traffic trouble and an unconsidered runner sneaks a clear run.
scenarios.body: Chaos at a hurdle or a fractured pace leaves a horse from the back half of the field with a clear passage while the principals interfere with each other. Given how compressed the midfield will be with multiple redistributed hold-up types, traffic incidents are a realistic if low-probability disruption to the dominant shape.

watchPoints.text: Ripsnorter (Danny Mullins) — if he meets every hurdle cleanly and is allowed to coast in front, the uncontested lead transforms this from a competitive handicap into a procession; watch his jumping at the first two flights as any early error invites Go To Town to press him.

Midfield congestion at the first hurdle — with seven horses redistributed from their natural hold-up position into a compressed midfield group, the opening flight in a 14-runner field on a tight Ballinrobe track carries a real risk of interference or a falling incident that reshapes the entire race.

Fremantle Doctor (161-day absence) — the long layoff for John McConnell's horse means fitness is unproven; if he runs flat or makes jumping errors early, he becomes a moving obstacle for the hold-up horses trying to navigate around him in a packed rear-to-midfield group.

Koeur A Prendre's finishing form — back-to-back 20f placings on Good give him an obvious late-race profile if the pace quickens sufficiently, but his true hold-up nature forced into midfield means watch whether Daniel King sits quietly and waits or is forced wider than ideal on the turn.

Go To Town's freshness angle — only 4 days since his last run is unusually tight and worth monitoring in the paddock; if he moves well pre-race the fitness is real and he represents the most credible challenge to Ripsnorter on race-shape grounds alone.

races.name: Broderick's Electric Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Grey Gardens
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up mare with a decent recent run at this trip on good ground 38 days ago; Paul Nolan stable has been quiet (0/10 in 14 days) but she handles this going and is a genuine closer who will need a stronger pace than The Toothpicker is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Consistent Slevin booking for Fahy but flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, and her recent form at this course distance (16th on good) is not encouraging; six-year-old hold-up type who has not placed in six good-ground runs, making her tough to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Let Him B
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good ground and placed at the trip, so the distance suits; a natural hold-up horse who has shown he can stay, but 74 days off and the fading flag temper enthusiasm — if fit, a pace that develops from three out plays to his strengths.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a headgear note (tongue tie visible), unseated last time; three places from 15 good-ground runs shows he handles the surface, but form reads cold and 39 days off with an undistinguished recent string makes him hard to rely on.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Won over this sort of trip on good ground and back within a week, suggesting connections are happy with his condition; Danny Mullins takes the ride for Thomas Mullins, which is always worth noting, but fading tendencies and the modest pace are negatives for a horse who needs the race to develop.

runners_data.name: Cool Summer
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose best run this season was a second over this trip on good ground; Flanagan aboard and the horse wears a hood — placed onto the map in midfield but likely to race further back than shown, which in a compressed field could cost him ground at the crucial point.

runners_data.name: Euro Maker
runners_data.note: Ran a promising second on good ground at 16f but 75 days off for a yard with a quiet strike rate; flagged as a fader and a natural closer whose redistribution to midfield means he is unlikely to get the clean passage his best form required — best watched before trusting.

runners_data.name: Sayitfirst
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 who has won and placed multiple times on good ground, including a win over 18f; 246 days off is a significant query and the redistribution note means he won't get the prominent position that saw his best efforts, but the form profile on this going is genuinely eye-catching if fit.

runners_data.name: Victoria Kesia
runners_data.note: Trainer Hanlon had a winner in the last 14 days (1/15) and this five-year-old has a place at 18f on good; natural hold-up type pushed onto the map in midfield, meaning she won't race where she wants to — last eight runs show no win on good ground and no pattern to suggest a different outcome here.

runners_data.name: The Toothpicker
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, wearing a tongue tie and 108 days off for a small yard; his recent string of consecutive fifths on good ground is consistent but uninspiring — his value is purely positional, as solo leader in a field of hold-up types his tactical advantage is real even if his raw ability is modest.

runners_data.name: All In Peder
runners_data.note: OR 84 hold-up type who has headgear (pads) and has been pulled up last time; Ricky Doyle rides for a cold Dempsey yard (0/0 in 14 days), 34 days off, and five recent finishes all in double figures — hard to make a case for, particularly racing out of his natural position.

runners_data.name: Spread The Faith
runners_data.note: McKiernan had two winners in 14 days (2/8) which is a positive flag; hold-up mare who fades and has pulled up three times in recent form — despite the trainer angle, the form figures are brutal and she is mapped away from her natural running position.

runners_data.name: Lunar Landscape
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who finished sixth last time on good ground, best recent effort; Thomas Coyle yard quiet (0/4 in 14 days) and the horse's true hold-up style means midfield mapping understates where she will likely race — Ballinrobe's tight circuit could suit if she can travel, but the form ceiling looks limited.

runners_data.name: Sidiriya
runners_data.note: Rothwell has been busy and productive (2/23 in 14 days) and this seven-year-old has placed three times on good ground including a second and third recently; natural hold-up type mapped to midfield, but the consistent good-ground form at this sort of trip makes her one of the more credible closers if the race develops late.

runners_data.name: Bangor Lady
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and has not placed in any of her six good-ground starts; Daniel King rides for a very cold Ryan yard (0/24 in 14 days), 17 days between runs — the redistribution from her natural hold-up position and the form record together make her very difficult to support.

runners_data.name: Western Doyen
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old returning from 643 days off, which is the most significant query in the race; Conor Stone-Walsh takes the ride for a small yard and he has placed on good ground before — genuinely prominent style means he gets his position, but that absence makes confidence impossible.

runners_data.name: Calm Flight Ahead
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has pulled up last time and whose only sim-going run produced a finish well back; Rothwell yard is in form but this horse wears blinkers, has been off 74 days and fades — the lack of any real good-going form (1/5) is the key concern alongside the redistribution away from her natural role.

runners_data.name: Ikalimix
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a tongue tie who fell last time and has not won or placed since 2022; O'Sullivan yard quiet (0/6) and the horse has been back within a week suggesting they are simply running him into form — hard to see how he competes off OR 95 with that profile.

runners_data.name: Moulane West
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with a tongue tie, back just four days after his last run which is unusually quick; McNiff yard quiet (0/5) and his good-ground record shows consistent finishes in the 9-12 range — a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield, the rapid turnaround is the most notable factor and rarely a positive sign at this level.

races.paceDynamic: The Toothpicker is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and should secure an uncontested lead from the front, setting a sustainable gallop around Ballinrobe's tight, undulating circuit without being seriously pressured for position. Western Doyen is the only other horse mapped prominently, and while he offers some nominal company, he is unlikely to push The Toothpicker hard enough to turn this into a true test of stamina. The overwhelming majority of the field — Grey Gardens, Home By The Sea, Let Him B, Max Meridius and many others — are natural hold-up types, meaning The Toothpicker can effectively dictate on his own terms from the front, controlling tempo and conserving energy through the early stages. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel efficiently in midfield and produce a sustained run from three out, as the even, unhurried gallop set by a lone leader will likely compress the field and reward horses with a high cruising speed rather than raw closing power. Several runners including Moulane West, Victoria Kesia, Sayitfirst and Cool Summer are genuine hold-up or prominent types redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; The Toothpicker and Western Doyen are most likely to actually secure their forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Toothpicker Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If The Toothpicker bowls along unchallenged and the field fails to close the gap approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: The Toothpicker dictates at a measured pace, his rivals sit in behind unable to quicken sufficiently off a flat tempo, and the gap he has built approaching the last proves decisive. Horses who travel prominently and don't need a strong pace to be at their best — particularly The Toothpicker himself and Western Doyen who get their natural positions — are the direct beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough that midfield horses with decent form on good ground mount a coordinated late challenge.
scenarios.body: The Toothpicker's lead is sustainable but not unassailable, and horses tracking in the first half of the chasing pack find enough momentum from three out to reel him in on the run-in. Horses with strong recent good-ground form and proven ability to finish off this trip — Let Him B, Max Meridius, Sidiriya — fit this shape best given their genuine hold-up credentials.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Two Clear The Rest
scenarios.trigger: If The Toothpicker and Western Doyen race prominently together and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: The two front-positioned horses race away from a moderate and disorganised chasing pack, with the large field of redirected hold-up types struggling to find racing room or momentum around Ballinrobe's tight turns. Western Doyen, 643 days off and making a significant return, would need to recapture something close to his best, making this a lower-probability but live shape given his on-paper prominent style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race is run in a rush early, causing The Toothpicker to stop and the genuine closers to come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A scenario that requires true hold-up horses to be racing in their natural position deep in the field, but most of the redistributed runners here are not genuine sit-and-sprint types and are likely to be crowded into midfield rather than tracking at the rear where a late run would be most effective. Grey Gardens, with her proven good-ground form from 38 days off and a decent recent run at this trip, is the most credible beneficiary among those mapped furthest back.

watchPoints.text: The Toothpicker's solo lead is the race's defining tactical factor — watch whether Western Doyen challenges him early, as if The Toothpicker gets even 3-4 lengths clear by the second flight the hold-up horses face a near-impossible task in a compressed gallop.

Sayitfirst is 246 days off the track and has a strong good-ground record including wins and multiple places — if he has been freshened for this specific target he could be significantly ahead of the market, but the layoff makes him a watch rather than a trust.

Sidiriya's trainer P J Rothwell has had 2 winners from 23 runners in the past 14 days and the horse has placed twice recently on good ground — monitor market moves, as a yard in form with a horse showing consistent placed form is a combination that sometimes arrives quietly.

Western Doyen returns from a 643-day absence; if he shows any unexpected market support in the minutes before the off it would suggest connections have him in better shape than the stats imply, given he is the only horse who can realistically take a prominent position alongside The Toothpicker.

The large number of redistributed hold-up horses (10+) means Ballinrobe's tight circuit could create serious traffic problems in the straight — watch for horses who can find a clear passage on the outer from three out, as those stuck behind a wall of horses may never get a clean run.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a poor recent string (8560-0) and zero wins or places on similar Good ground in two runs; John McConnell stable in fair nick (2/29 T14) but this 8-year-old at 166lbs looks up against it from the rear over 3m2f with a genuinely uncontested leader to chase.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type whose four-run Good-ground sample shows two places (0W2P) — solid consistency without a win; Jack Gilligan's 5lb claim is useful at 161lbs and the 12-day turnaround for Paul John Gilligan (1/15 T14) is fine, though finishing in the mix will require a step up.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Travels in headgear (tp) and has a strong Good-ground profile (13/15 sim-going, 1W5P) with genuine stamina credentials at 24f-plus — however this is a natural come-from-behind horse whose true style sits further back than the midfield slot shown, and with three genuine hold-up types crowding the rear, its chance hinges on finding clean air it may not get.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has finished 6th, 7th, or 8th in five of his last five starts; the tp headgear does little to disguise modest form (76-867), and although he is a legitimate hold-up type he cannot take his preferred position freely here — Curling has had no runners in 14 days (0/7) adding further caution.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field and therefore controls the race shape entirely; an 87-day absence is the primary concern for Brian McMahon's charge, and a flat recent record (67U5-6) on Good ground suggests little margin for error, but the tactical advantage of racing alone on the front end is substantial at 3m2f.

runners_data.name: Down Around
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's nine-year-old wears a hood (b) and has a solid Good-ground record (13/15 sim-going, 1W4P) with a placed effort over 22f at Southwell in recent form — naturally prominent, Sam Ewing can slot comfortably into second or third from the outset and exploit the uncontested pace scenario directly.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Returned just four days ago (LR:4d) which is a short turnaround worth flagging; a natural hold-up horse whose recent form shows genuine placing ability (57-324) on Good and Soft — but like Dorans Law it is being pressed into midfield rather than its natural rear berth, and the style-fit discount moderates its claims accordingly.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old in tongue-tie (t) for Norman Lee with an excellent Good-ground profile (14/15 sim-going, 1W7P) and consistent placed form at 20-22f — naturally prominent, Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim brings the weight to a manageable 142lbs, and the horse's ability to track the pace from the outset makes it one of the better-placed runners for this race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Strange Currency is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will control the gallop entirely on their own terms over 3m2f of Good ground at Ballinrobe. That lone-leader dynamic creates a sustainable, measured pace rather than a pressured one — Strange Currency can bowl along at a rhythm that preserves their stamina reserves and makes life difficult for anything held up far off the bridle. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear: Dorans Law, Lord Ffrench, and Run For The Border are genuine come-from-behind horses who have been mapped to midfield but are unlikely to secure that position naturally, meaning the true backmarkers are crowded and any winner from that group must overcome an unfamiliar positional squeeze. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a controlled tempo over a stiff 3m2f — classically favours prominent racers who can track the pace comfortably and pounce in the straight, with Down Around and Ladiam best placed positionally, while deep closers face the most ground to find.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strange Currency Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Strange Currency jumps cleanly, dictates a steady gallop, and no prominent horse applies sustained pressure in the first mile.
scenarios.body: Strange Currency sets a comfortable rhythm with Down Around and Ladiam in his slipstream, and if the fractions are generous the leader can conserve enough to hold on into the straight; the prominent pair tracking just off the pace are perfectly placed to challenge in the final two flights.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Down Around or Ladiam track Strange Currency closely and use their superior class or fitness edge to collar the leader approaching the last.
scenarios.body: The leader is reeled in from two out as the prominent horses, never far off the pace, produce their effort without needing an extra gear; the Good ground and 3m2f trip suits those who conserve energy in midpack before asserting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops a stronger early pace than expected and the closers pick off the fading field in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Dorans Law or Run For The Border, despite being pressed into a midfield role rather than their natural rear position, still get into the race late if something goes wrong for the leaders; however both are racing out of their natural role and the style-fit discount is significant, limiting confidence here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Strange Currency goes too slow early, triggering a chaotic dash for home that scrambles the predicted order.
scenarios.body: In a falsely-run race any horse positioned handily can steal a march on rivals floundering for their ground; Killowen House or My Trump Card, each with some form at the trip on Good going, could sneak into the money if the finish turns messy and muddling.

watchPoints.text: Strange Currency's 87-day absence is the single biggest risk to the dominant scenario — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness at the first few flights that could unsettle the pace plan entirely.

Dorans Law, Lord Ffrench, and Run For The Border are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same limited rear-field space; watch for early jostling and traffic issues in the back straight as they cannot all settle in their preferred position.

Down Around's hood (b) and Gordon Elliott's prominent-runner profile means this horse is likely to be sent forward early — watch whether Sam Ewing attempts to sit upsides Strange Currency or tucks in second, as that decision shapes the entire race.

Ladiam's tongue-tie (t) combined with a 5lb claim for O'Sullivan keeps the weight low at 142lbs — watch whether the yard (1/1 T14) has tuned the horse up with this race specifically in mind given the light recent strike rate.

The Good ground has been consistent all evening across every Ballinrobe race — no hidden pace bias or deteriorating surface to consider, so form at this going is a reliable guide and horses with strong Good-ground profiles (Dorans Law, Ladiam, Down Around) hold their profile fully.

races.name: Bay Leaf Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Barton Sky
runners_data.note: Veteran handicapper for Hanlon, finished placed last time at Goodwood (5th/2nd recent), handles Good ground fine, but is a genuine hold-up operator and will find the midfield much more competitive than his natural rear position — 17 days since last run is fine, but style is a concern here.

runners_data.name: Boomerang Breeze
runners_data.note: Timothy Doyle-trained eight-year-old who has finished 9th and 10th in his last two Good-ground starts and is flagged for fading in the finish — dropped into midfield by the map though he wants to be further back, and that blend of fading tendency and crowded late ground makes this very difficult.

runners_data.name: Derby Rock
runners_data.note: Amateur-ridden (Mr P A King, 3lb claim) for a small yard with no recent runners, seven-year-old who has consistently filled mid-to-rear positions and pulled up on his latest start — the map has him in midfield but he naturally wants the rear, and his form figures offer little hope at any trip.

runners_data.name: Gainsville
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old with an unknown style tag and lightly-raced flag — the trainer's 4/35 14-day strike rate adds some confidence, and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking; finished 6th and 9th on similar Good ground but placed twice in bumpers, making this trip genuinely unexplored territory.

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: J J Slevin, a top jumps jockey, is the obvious draw here, but the horse has finished 6th or 7th in four of his last five Good-ground starts and is a dedicated hold-up type squeezed into midfield — Slevin may get a better position than the map suggests, but the form trail is stubborn.

runners_data.name: Keep Em Quite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Cian Collins, 86 days off (longest break in the field), placed twice from four starts on similar ground — sits naturally just off the pace which is the ideal profile in this shape, though the layoff and lowly OR of 102 are queries at this level.

runners_data.name: Kilmond Knight
runners_data.note: Only six days since his last run (shortest in the field) for David Barry — the quick turnaround needs monitoring; mapped to midfield but genuinely wants to be held up, and his form of P-U07 includes a fall and a pulled-up, suggesting jumping reliability is the primary concern.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Power-trained five-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and three consecutive Good-ground runs finishing 6th, 10th and 13th — a hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution, and with no visible improvement in form the profile is unpromising at 2m6½f.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: Rothwell-trained five-year-old, 65 days off, ran a noteworthy 1st at 18f on Good ground among his recent efforts — natural hold-up runner who ideally needs the rear but could benefit if the Ballinrobe straight suits a one-run stayer; the winning form is the standout positive here.

runners_data.name: Three County Star
runners_data.note: Brian Mortell yard with no runners in the last 14 days, seven-year-old amateur-ridden by Conor Smithers (7lb claim); flags a fade in the finish and has recorded double-figure finishes in most recent starts — the style redistribution compounds an already weak form profile.

runners_data.name: Likeyouhaveplenty
runners_data.note: Sean O'Brien-trained five-year-old, 35 days off, has finished 13th and 17th in his last two runs including on Good ground — fade-in-finish flag is consistent with that form, and the drop to 159lbs offers minor weight relief but the raw evidence is very discouraging.

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends a lightly-raced five-year-old (just two runs, 6th and 9th) with Brian Hayes aboard — the combination of stable, jockey quality and unknown ceiling makes this one of the more interesting unexposed profiles in the race despite modest visible form.

runners_data.name: Secret Moon
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon second string, five-year-old who has been beaten 8th, 6th and 8th in all three starts, flagged both lightly raced and as a fader — Josh Younge takes the ride; the form is modest but the unexposed angle keeps a small question mark open.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's five-year-old returns after just 12 days and wears a hood (headgear noted) — finished 32nd and 14th recently, is flagged as a fader, and tends towards the rear though mapped to hold-up; nothing in the recent record suggests competitive improvement.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends Jack Kennedy, the best jockey-trainer combination in the field among the hold-up group, and this five-year-old has placed 5th, 5th and 6th in three consecutive Good-ground starts showing consistent if unspectacular form — a genuine hold-up type shifted to midfield by the crowded map, Kennedy may manufacture a better position.

runners_data.name: Go To The Moon
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in a 16-runner field, controlling the gallop entirely unchallenged over 2m6½f of Good ground for Mark McNiff — wears tongue-tie, 35 days since last run, and the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage, though a 7th and 12th in last two starts suggests the horse must convert opportunity into performance.

races.paceDynamic: Go To The Moon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — this horse will control the gallop from flag to finish at a pace entirely of its own choosing over 2m6½f of Good ground at Ballinrobe. With no rival capable of applying early pressure, the tempo is likely to be honest but manageable, creating a classic lone-leader scenario where the front-runner dictates every change of pace and can preserve energy for the final jumps. The bulk of the field — Kilmond Knight, Hey Sir, Boomerang Breeze, Barton Sky, Western Shores and others — are true hold-up types who have been pushed into a mapped midfield position simply because there is no room at the rear; in reality, this field is stacked with closers who will all be hunting the same late ground. That concentration of hold-up horses making their move simultaneously on the long Ballinrobe run-in actually benefits the uncontested leader, as the closers will interfere with one another — this race shape strongly favours prominent or close-tracking runners who can sit just off Go To The Moon and pounce before the hold-up brigade can organise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Go To The Moon bowls along uncontested and sets a tempo that is just strong enough to stretch the closers without burning itself out.
scenarios.body: Go To The Moon controls every fraction unchallenged, and any horse travelling fluently in second or third — such as Keep Em Quite — will be ideally placed to challenge only if the leader falters at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or close-tracking type sits within two lengths of Go To The Moon throughout and outstays it from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The race is run at a tempo that is sustainable enough for a well-positioned stalker to grab the leader's slipstream and kick clear; Gainsville (unknown style, De Bromhead) and Room For One More (Mullins) are the most plausible profiles to capitalise from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinder Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the leader ties up late, allowing a one-paced hold-up type to grind past close home.
scenarios.body: Despite the redistribution caveat, a genuine stayer running out of role in midfield — such as Western Shores (Elliott, Jack Kennedy, consistent Good-ground form) or Barton Sky — could pick up the pieces if the front group all burn brightly too soon.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is falsely slow early then injected sharply at the top of the home straight, causing carnage in the jumping ranks.
scenarios.body: A truly messy race with multiple errors under a surging pace would randomly elevate any horse still jumping cleanly at the last; Scotty Joe or Kilmond Knight might inherit a result, but this scenario relies on a specific race-shape unlikely with a lone, measured front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Go To The Moon is uncontested up front and will control the tempo completely — watch whether the pace is genuinely honest or so slow that it sets up a sprint finish that even the holder-uppers can win.

Jack Kennedy on Western Shores is the standout jockey-on-a-hold-up-type combination — watch for Kennedy to engineer a position much closer to the pace than the map suggests, effectively turning a hold-up horse into a close tracker.
Kilmond Knight runs just six days after his last start, the quickest turnaround in the field — monitor at the overnight scratchings stage and watch for any signs of fatigue in the jumping early on.

The sheer volume of redistributed hold-up horses (eight or more genuine closers all hunting the same late ground) means the home straight at Ballinrobe could be extremely congested — horses with the best jumps at the final two flights will have a decisive edge over those who need a clear passage.

Room For One More (Mullins/Hayes) and Gainsville (De Bromhead/O'Keeffe) represent the two most powerful unexposed profiles whose true ceiling is unknown — watch market moves in the hour before the off as these yards rarely send horses blind.

races.name: Tim Kelly Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type in good heart — won over this course at 22f on good and has solid recent form figures of 1-3; 58 days off is not a concern for this handler and Phillip Enright rides.|

runners_data.name: Cornaroya Rocco
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up runner returning quickly on 25 days; best recent effort was a 2nd at 20f on good, and the step up to 2m6½f is the key question given three of last five runs were over 16f.|

runners_data.name: Tannery Park
runners_data.note: 440 days off the track is a significant flag even with a good record on similar going; Sean Flanagan takes the ride for Barry Connell but the fitness query after such a long absence is hard to ignore, and he carries a 'fades in finish' warning.|

runners_data.name: The Little Yank
runners_data.note: Consistent veteran hold-up horse with back-to-back 3rds over 25f on good ground; ran just two days ago which warrants scrutiny, and the 7lb claimer John Aherne partners him in a competitive 19-runner handicap.|

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with a 'fades in finish' flag; showed a 2nd at 24f on good last time but has two very poor efforts either side and the headgear addition (p) may sharpen him, Mr Sugrue claims 7lbs.|

runners_data.name: Political Stance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner 146 days off the track; best effort recently was a 2nd at 16f on heavy, and neither the distance nor the return from such a long break makes this straightforward.|

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent-type who should be in the first three or four throughout; ten-year-old wearing headgear (p), ran 20 days ago, and his record of 1 win and 4 places from 13 runs at this track/distance/going combination is eye-catching.|

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent runner returning 20 days after his last start; J J Slevin is a significant booking and he has 2 wins and 4 places from 12 similar-going runs, making him a consistent if ageing yardstick.|

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: In truth a hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map because the rear is overpopulated — recent form of 13th, 5th, 7th offers little encouragement and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations materially.|

runners_data.name: Chanceitlucky
runners_data.note: Returns after 267 days off — the lengthy break alone makes this a risky proposition; a genuine hold-up type operating out of role in midfield due to the high density of closers, and the 'fades in finish' flag compounds the concern.|

runners_data.name: Moonshine Girl
runners_data.note: Form figures of 2-2-7 over 22-24f on good suggest she retains ability, with headgear (p) fitted; a true hold-up runner crowded into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, which blunts her most effective tactical weapon.|

runners_data.name: Urbs Intacta Manet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a 'fades in finish' tendency and headgear (p); 89 days off, limited form on good ground (2 from 6), and being a natural hold-up type forced into midfield makes her winning prospects modest.|

runners_data.name: Mini Getaway
runners_data.note: Prominent-type with a tidy record of 3rds and 4ths at 22-24f on good and heavy; 94 days off may mean peak fitness is still a run away, but the profile of a patient front-racer suits this pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: A horse whose recent form reads 11th, 8th, 12th on good ground; 17 days since last run, the 'fades in finish' flag and an honest hold-up style pushed into midfield combine to make this very difficult.|

runners_data.name: Queen Kulina
runners_data.note: Prominent ten-year-old with two 2nds and a 3rd from 13 runs at 24f on good; Shane O'Callaghan (3lb claimer) rides and she shows up consistently at this trip, making her a durable each-way profile.|

runners_data.name: La Tene
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two recent 3rds at 22f and 19f on good and soft; trainer John Patrick Ryan also saddles The Little Yank and the dual runner angle is worth noting — 20 days since last run, Michael Kenneally claims 5lbs.|

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose best recent effort is a 5th at 22f on good; no jockey listed which is an obvious concern, and a natural hold-up profile squeezed out by the redistribution makes the winning chance very limited.|

runners_data.name: Everystep Oftheway
runners_data.note: Off the track for 763 days — that is an extraordinary lay-off for an eight-year-old; a true hold-up horse mapped forward due to field density, and without any recent racecourse evidence it is almost impossible to assess current ability.|

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and race-shaper, likely to lead from the off on good ground over 2m6½f; STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is a modest caution, but nine-year-old with a win at 21f on soft and has run 20 days ago.|

races.paceDynamic: Joshua Chamberlain is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and should lead from the outset over 2m6½f on good ground at Ballinrobe, setting a measured, uncontested tempo that suits those who can travel just off the pace rather than those making up ground late. It's Time Again and Ranger Billy are the likeliest horses to press him from a prominent position, though neither has the natural dominance to seriously disrupt his rhythm, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Poetic Focus, Everystep Oftheway, Chanceitlucky, Moonshine Girl, La Tene and others are true hold-up horses who will be forced to race closer to midfield than is their preference, diluting their finishing effectiveness. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner, a manageable gallop, good ground — strongly favours prominent-racing types who can travel in Joshua Chamberlain's slipstream and pick up fluently in the straight, rather than closers who will find the late sectionals insufficiently strong to reel them in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chamberlain Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Joshua Chamberlain leads unchallenged at a fair gallop and those immediately tracking him hold a winning position turning for home.
scenarios.body: Joshua Chamberlain dictates the fractions, keeping the race honest enough that the prominent chasers — It's Time Again, Ranger Billy, Mini Getaway — are always travelling and can pounce without needing a genuine test of stamina. The sustainable pace means fitness and jumping fluency at the business end count more than a late turn of foot, rewarding those who race in the first half-dozen.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Forced Wide, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the prominent horses sit so close that the redistributed hold-up types are squeezed out and cannot quicken from deep.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo compresses the field and those redistributed to midfield — Poetic Focus, Moonshine Girl, Everystep Oftheway — never find a clear run, leaving the race to be decided by horses up with the pace who stay on strongly. Nothing Hectic and Cornaroya Rocco, the highest-rated hold-up runners with genuine finishing ability, are among the few closers equipped to navigate traffic and still threaten.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test, Distance Suits Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens mid-race or the field strings out over the 2m6½f trip, exposing horses short of stamina.
scenarios.body: The longer distance begins to sort out genuine stayers from those who are better over shorter, and horses with a proven record at this trip or further come into their own late on. The Little Yank and La Tene, both with solid form at 22f-25f on good ground, could prove durable enough to grind out places even from deep positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Blows Up, Outsiders Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the unusually large 19-runner field produces early scrimmaging, fallers or interference that scrambles the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Disruption early on would reshuffle positions and create gaps, potentially allowing horses who find clean air to steal a march on those hampered in traffic. Queen Kulina and Mini Getaway, consistent prominent types with course-trip form on good ground, carry the profile to capitalise if the principals are inconvenienced.

watchPoints.text: Everystep Oftheway — 763 days off the track is unprecedented in this field; connections of anything in his path should be alert to a rusty jumper who may make errors early in a 19-runner field.
The Little Yank — ran just two days ago and partnered by a 7lb claimer in a 19-runner handicap; watch for any sign of fatigue or erratic jumping that could cause interference in traffic.
Tannery Park — 440 days absent returning in a highly competitive handicap; a horse returning after such a long lay-off can make jumping errors at pace and jockeys tracking him should be cautious.

Joshua Chamberlain's pace — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at the head of affairs the gallop may be deceptively slow early, compressing the field and creating a traffic problem for the many hold-up types forced to race in midfield.

Large-field scrimmaging at the first hurdle — with 19 runners over 2m6½f at Ballinrobe, the initial jostle for position could disrupt horses like Poetic Focus and Moonshine Girl who are already racing out of their preferred hold-up role.
